title: Changing the report bill range erased contact fields
expected: Contact fields retain their values.
actual: The form remounted and cleared contact values.
impact: Users could lose work immediately before conversion.
recommendation: Keep bill-range state local to the form and avoid parent remounts.

title: Panel count disagreed across map, KPIs, and AI advisor
steps: Compare the map panel count, dashboard panel count, system size, and advisor summary
expected: Every surface uses the selected module's fitted panel count.
actual: The map and KPIs showed 20 while module-fit advisor copy used 19.
impact: A visible numerical contradiction undermined trust.
recommendation: Clamp shared active panel state and all consumers to the selected module's usable capacity.

title: Production-mode CSP upgraded local WebKit assets to HTTPS
steps: Build the application in production mode
expected: Local production-mode QA loads styles while deployed production retains HTTPS upgrade protection.
actual: WebKit attempted HTTPS for local assets and failed TLS.
impact: Safari/WebKit QA rendered an unstyled page and produced false failures.
recommendation: Enable upgrade-insecure-requests only in the Vercel production environment.

title: Satellite map used aria-label without a semantic role
steps: Run Axe on the roof analysis
expected: The map has a valid role and accessible description.
actual: The aria-label was attached to a generic div.
impact: Assistive technology could miss the map purpose.
recommendation: Use role=img with the descriptive aria-label and preserve a textual summary.

title: Report and roof tabs lacked complete ARIA relationships
steps: Keyboard to a roof or report tab
expected: Each tab identifies its controlled tabpanel.
actual: Tab roles existed without complete id and aria-controls relationships.
impact: Screen-reader context was weaker than the visual relationship.
recommendation: Use stable tab ids, aria-controls, role=tabpanel, and aria-labelledby.

title: Dashboard token inputs had no accessible labels
steps: Inspect the token field accessible name
expected: Token inputs have visible programmatic labels.
actual: The fields relied on surrounding copy and placeholder behavior.
impact: Assistive-technology users could not identify the credential field reliably.
recommendation: Associate labels and ids, mark required, and provide appropriate autocomplete.

title: Roof analysis loading progress was not announced
expected: Changing analysis progress is announced politely.
actual: Progress was visual only.
impact: Screen-reader users could not tell that work was continuing.
recommendation: Wrap progress in a polite status region.

title: Escape did not dismiss in-flight address results
steps: Press Escape before the response completes
expected: The popup remains dismissed.
actual: Late results reopened the popup.
impact: Keyboard recovery felt unpredictable.
recommendation: Track explicit dismissal and ignore stale responses.

title: Brand logo linked to an empty fragment
expected: The logo navigates to the homepage.
actual: It targeted #.
impact: Navigation was inconsistent and did not reset the route.
recommendation: Use the framework link to /.

title: Formal retention schedule and self-service deletion are missing
steps: Look for retention period and deletion workflow
expected: Users can understand retention and request or complete deletion.
actual: The notice states that a formal schedule and self-service workflow are not yet implemented.
impact: Creates a major privacy and trust gap.
recommendation: Define retention, add verified deletion/access requests, and document fulfillment.

title: Dashboard mutation failures are silent
steps: Cause a status or note mutation to fail
expected: The rollback is accompanied by a visible error and retry path.
actual: State rolls back without actionable user feedback.
impact: Installers may believe work was saved when it was not.
recommendation: Add an aria-live error toast and retry action.

title: Marketing follow-up consent path is unreachable
expected: If marketing follow-up is supported, users can explicitly opt in.
actual: The public flow safely leaves marketing consent false with no opt-in control.
impact: Marketing follow-up cannot be lawfully activated through the current UI.
recommendation: Either keep marketing disabled or add a separate unselected explicit consent control after legal review.

title: Financial model omits decision-critical assumptions
steps: Look for tariff, export, degradation, fees, and maintenance
expected: Decision-critical assumptions are visible or explicitly excluded.
actual: Several assumptions are absent or only partially disclosed.
impact: Long-term savings may be interpreted with more precision than the model supports.
recommendation: Add a consolidated assumptions/exclusions table without presenting it as an offer.

title: Installer cannot correct roof geometry or layout
steps: Attempt to edit planes, obstructions, setbacks, or panel positions
expected: An installer-oriented workflow can flag or correct model errors.
actual: Only high-level panel count and display layers are adjustable.
impact: The product remains a homeowner preview rather than an installer assessment.
recommendation: Add a future installer correction workflow with revision provenance.

title: Component-level calculation paths can drift from shared metrics
steps: Trace map, dashboard, report, and submission calculations
expected: Every displayed and submitted value derives from one canonical snapshot.
actual: A shared model exists, but some component-specific financing and display calculations remain.
impact: Future changes can reintroduce mismatched values.
recommendation: Complete the canonical report snapshot migration and add cross-surface contract tests.

title: Pending upload cleanup depends on external scheduling
steps: Inspect the pending upload cleanup route and deployment scheduling
expected: Uploads older than the retention window are deleted automatically and monitored.
actual: The cleanup route exists but requires an external cron configuration.
impact: Orphaned personal documents may persist if scheduling is absent.
recommendation: Configure Vercel Cron, alert on failures, and verify bucket lifecycle rules.

title: Homepage support path is not prominent
steps: Look for help or support contact without opening legal pages
expected: A visible support path is available near the footer or report request.
actual: The support email is available in legal pages but not prominent in the main journey.
impact: Cautious users may abandon rather than ask a question.
recommendation: Add a low-emphasis support link to the footer.

title: Production is behind the tested local fix set
steps: Compare the logo destination and tested local behavior
expected: Production serves the tested commit.
actual: Production still showed the pre-fix logo destination.
impact: Verified fixes do not benefit live users until deployed.
recommendation: Deploy the tested commit and rerun the production read-only smoke suite.

title: Rate-limit documentation differs from implementation
steps: Compare README route limits with source limit configuration
expected: Documented limits match deployed behavior.
actual: Some documented windows and thresholds differ from source.
impact: Support and incident response may set incorrect expectations.
recommendation: Generate the README table from shared route-limit constants or update it in the same change.

title: Empty address action looks enabled
steps: Open the homepage with an empty address
expected: The action is disabled or explains what is required.
actual: The arrow appears actionable before a valid selection exists.
impact: Users may click with no visible result and hesitate.
recommendation: Use a disabled state tied to a selected valid address and preserve keyboard guidance.

title: High-severity transitive PostCSS and Sharp advisories remain
expected: No unresolved high-severity production advisories.
actual: Next 16.2.12 removes direct framework advisories, but npm still reports bundled PostCSS and Sharp findings.
impact: Potential file disclosure or image-processing risk remains depending on reachable code paths.
recommendation: Track patched compatible releases, assess route reachability, and do not apply npm's unsafe Next 9 downgrade.

title: Report validation errors lacked a focused summary
steps: Submit the empty form with the keyboard
expected: Keyboard and screen-reader users land on a concise error summary with links to each invalid field.
actual: The form focused the first invalid control without summarizing all validation errors.
impact: Users had to search a long form to understand and recover from multiple validation errors.
recommendation: Focus an accessible error summary and provide links to each invalid control while preserving field-level errors.
